newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's CVRD seen sold 20-30 pct above base price.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's CVRD seen sold 20-30 pct above base price.

text.p: Brazil's market analysts expect state miner Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) to be sold 20 percent to 30 percent above its base price when it is auctioned off on April 29, a local newspaper said.

The Gazeta Mercantil newspaper said analysts see fierce competition between the two groups of investors which registered with the Rio de Janeiro bolsa to qualify for the auction of a 40-45 percent voting stake in CVRD, which will be sold for a minimum 3.0 billion reais ($2.83 billion).
One consortium is Valecom, led by local metal, cement, steel and pulp and paper conglomerate Grupo Votorantim and South Africa's Anglo-American Corp, which has a strong Japanese presence.
The other group of investors, called Valepar, is led by Brazilian private steelmaker CSN and comprises U.S. aluminium company Alcoa, NationsBank, local pension funds and banks.

In an interview to Jornal do Brasil newspaper today, Votorantim president Antonio Ermirio de Moraes guaranteed that the Valecom consortium will maintain the CVRD system as it is if the group wins the auction.
Moraes told the paper he believes Valecom has more synergy with CVRD as Votorantim and Anglo American are in the mining business.
The Votorantim president, who has said will head CVRD's Administrative Council if the group wins, also criticized those who allege that Vale was undervalued.
"If (Vale) was really undervalued, there would be some 50 groups interested in buying it," he was quoted as saying.
Moraes also said the CVRD deal will set the future of Votorantim group.
"We are now a family business, but our future is to be a publicly traded company. The purchase of Vale is the first step in this direction," he told Jornal do Brasil.
